title: 4 days Body parts split program review
summary: NH tears apart a viewer's 4-day body part split that opens and closes every day with 15-rep deadlifts, uses single sets and piles up redundant curls, flies and ab variations. He explains why high-rep deadlifts are junk volume and rewrites it as a 3-4 day upper/lower plan with supersets and proper deadlift prescriptions.
claims: An arm day must be earned: first train legs at least twice a week and do plenty of upper back work
There is no such thing as a chest day; do lower body days instead of leg days, and a once-a-week leg day is no good
He has never seen presses and pulls programmed well on the same shoulder-and-back day
An arm day should add upper body compounds, never lower body lifts like deadlifts
An 8-15 rep range is too wide: if you can get 15 you will almost always get 12-13
Superset curls; people with small arms often train two hours but only 40 minutes is actual work and the rest is resting
Stacking biceps exercises is for advanced lifters; three sets to failure in a relevant rep range beat six random sets, and he himself uses at most two biceps exercises a day
Barbell curls, the most overloadable curl, should not be done last
Keep conventional deadlifts at 5 reps or fewer; RDLs suit higher reps; the deadlift takes little time and does not need high frequency to progress
Novices burn out mentally before physically, so keep their sessions short
Allow at least 48 hours between an arm day and a following upper body day
A pump alone will not build bigger arms; apply intensity to them as you would to legs
Single sets per exercise are not conducive to hypertrophy; use set multiplication
Cleans need so much technique and warm-up that they need a specific justification; there are better hypertrophy tools
For abs pick one or two bracing and one or two stretching exercises and multiply sets instead of doing many variations
3-6 reps is a good range for the overhead press but needs at least three sets
15-rep deadlifts are pure junk volume: the structure fails before the muscle, so aim for form degradation without breakdown and stop around 5-6 reps
Four sets of 8-12 reps of chest flies is all you need
Corrected upper day: bench, then overhead press supersetted with chin-ups, then curls supersetted with skull crushers and lateral raises or rear delt flies, then abs and calves
Corrected lower day: squats 3-4 sets of 6-10, RDL supersetted with pull-ups (8-12 and max reps), then calves, abs and optional back extensions, alternating heavy squat or heavy deadlift emphasis
Second upper day: overhead press, close-grip bench, then supersets of shrugs, forearms, abs and calves; run it as 3 or 4 days a week
Deadlift prescription: 1-3 sets of 2-5 reps, or even one set, followed by backup sets
exercises: quick high-quality tonnage; 15 reps is junk
higher reps fine due to modified strength curve
most overloadable curl, do not end with it
too technical for hypertrophy without justification
horizontal press variation for second upper
